stem_book: The negative value of electronic energy in a Bohr orbit implies that: (a) The electron is bound to the nucleus and has less energy than a free electron (b) The electron is unstable and will leave the atom (c) The electron possesses more energy than a free electron (d) The electron is in an excited unbound state
key: a The electron is bound to the nucleus and has less energy than a free electron
derived: a The electron is bound to the nucleus and has less energy than a free electron
correct_answer: a The electron is bound to the nucleus and has less energy than a free electron
work: Free electron at n = ∞ has E = 0; E_n = −13.6Z²/n² < 0 ⇒ bound, lower energy than free
